finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF and local file read via file_get_contents() on a raw POST parameter. Any visitor can make the server fetch an arbitrary URI, including internal HTTP services and file://, php://, or phar:// URIs.
finding.source: import.php:11 — $_POST['feed'] (no auth, no type or format check)

trace.note: Branch taken when REQUEST_METHOD is POST and 'feed' is set. require_admin() is not called on this branch.
file_get_contents() receives the attacker string as-is and fetches it. PHP stream wrappers and http redirects are followed.
Only strlen($xml) is echoed. The body is not returned, so exfiltration is a length oracle. A failed fetch may still leak through PHP warnings if display_errors is on.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host or IP denylist, DNS pinning, port restriction, redirect limit, or auth check on this path. require_admin() guards only the set_webhook branch. The only conditional is the POST and isset check. Whether allow_url_fopen is enabled is a deployment setting not visible in this file; if it is disabled, http(s) fetches fail but file:// reads still work.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only conditional on the path is import.php:11 (POST and isset($_POST['feed'])). require_admin() at import.php:4-9 is only called on the set_webhook branch at import.php:18, and nothing before the sink at import.php:12 validates the scheme, host, or port.
verdict.reason: import.php:11 takes $_POST['feed'] with no auth check, and import.php:12 passes it unvalidated to file_get_contents(), so any unauthenticated visitor can fetch an arbitrary URI or read local files, with only strlen() echoed back at import.php:13.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF via libcurl. The set_webhook value is used as the request URL without any scheme or host validation, and the response body is discarded.

trace.note: require_admin() checks $_SESSION['is_admin']. Anything other than an empty value passes, and nothing in this file sets it.
$hook is assigned directly from the POST value.
curl_init($hook) uses the string as CURLOPT_URL. libcurl's default protocol set includes file://, gopher://, ftp://, and others.
RETURNTRANSFER is set, but the return value of curl_exec is discarded. The response is never echoed, so the attack is blind.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() is the only check. It is an authorization gate, not URL validation, so the URL itself is unconstrained. No CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS_STR or CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction, no host or IP filter, and no redirect cap (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is not set, so redirects are not followed). Admin is required, so exposure is limited to admins or to anyone who can forge the is_admin session value.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 is an authorization check only. No URL, scheme, or host validation, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction, and no CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION set anywhere in the directory. It does not close the URL sink, but it does restrict the source to admins.
verdict.reason: The trace at import.php:17-22 is accurate, but the source is not attacker-controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege user: import.php:18 calls require_admin(), which exits with 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is set (import.php:5-7). The candidate's "forge the is_admin session value" path is unsupported by the code, since the session is server-side and nothing in the directory shows a forgery route. Exposure is limited to admins, which is the admin-only case the verifier rules exclude. The unauthenticated `feed` branch at import.php:11-13 is a separate issue and is not covered by this finding.
